Incorrect API quantity stated on the master formula for Quetiapine BMRs

The quantity of API powder established on the master formula of QUET2 BMR (Quetiapine 25 mg/5ml Oral Suspension) was incorrect and was potentially double the required strength.
This was raised with QA Management, who subsequently verified that the quantity of API specified in the master formula for all quetiapine BMRs (QUET1, QUET2, QUET3, QUET4, QUET5 and QUET7) was double what it should be.
Immediate actions taken are detailed in Section 3 of this deviation report and include quarantine and containment of all affected batches of product.

On 05-MAR-2026, a stability sample of Acetic Acid 2% Ear Drops, Batch STAB1125-001, stored under 25 °C/60 % RH conditions at Marfleet Analytical Services, was received by the Eaststone QC Department. Upon receipt and verification, it was identified that the sample provided was incorrectly labelled as “SPARE” instead of the required T3 stability timepoint sample.
It was therefore determined that the SPARE stability sample had been inadvertently pulled and transported in place of the requested T3 timepoint sample.
No temperature data during transit of Stability sample Mexiletine Hydrochloride Capsules 50mg

WHO: 
The deviation involves the person responsible for the coordination (Sunil Patel) and shipment of the stability samples (Charlotte Pryor). Validation Scientist, Sunil Patel from Eaststone Ltd decided to use FedEx as the transport provider (guaranteed next day delivery) as used by Marfleet Analytical Services Ltd, the contracted storage site for Eaststone stability samples.
WHAT: 
No temperature data was recorded during transit of stability samples. Although a Tinytag Ultra 2 data logger was included within the shipping container, it did not capture any temperature or humidity data during shipment period. This resulted in a lack of evidence to confirm the storage conditions of the stability samples during transit.
WHEN: 
The shipping container, including the data logger was received at Marfleet on 18-March-2026. The data logger was configured to begin recording on 23-March-2026 at 05:00, which is after the shipment had already taken place. Sample retrieval was originally scheduled for 23-March-2026, with return expected on 24-March-2026; however, the samples were instead shipped on their actual pull date of 19-March-2026 and returned on the following day 20-March-2026 before 13:00.
WHERE: 
The deviation occurred during transit between the dispatch site, Marfleet Analytical Services Ltd and the receiving site Eaststone Ltd, where the shipping container and data logger were delivered without any recorded transit temperature data.

customer requested Melatonin 2mg/5ml Oral suspension but ab oral solution BMR was generated and manufactured

Melatonin 2mg/5ml oral solution (BN ES180330) was manufactured on 07 Apr 2026 following receipt of a customer order requesting Melatonin 2mg/5ml oral suspension. However, during order processing, the BMR generator incorrectly generated a Batch Manufacturing Record (BMR) for the oral solution instead of the requested oral suspension.
The BMR verifier failed to identify this error and approved the incorrect BMR for manufacture. As a result, the batch was produced as an oral solution in line with the generated BMR rather than the customer’s requested oral suspension.
The error was not identified during any in-process checks and remained undetected until Final Release, where NAD identified that the manufactured product did not match the customer’s original request. The batch was subsequently rejected.
No QA/independent  review of stabilty timepoints

On 13APR26, it was identified that stability data for products is not routinely reviewed by Quality Assurance (QA) at each scheduled testing timepoint, and is instead only subject to final review upon completion of the study by the Head of Quality. This indicates that interim stability results are not being formally assessed or documented during the ongoing stability study lifecycle.

As a result, there is a potential gap in the timely identification of results, Out-Of-Specification (OOS) or Out-Of-Trend (OOT) results, which could delay appropriate investigation and escalation. This practice is not fully aligned with expectations for continuous monitoring of stability data to ensure ongoing product quality, patient safety and regulatory compliance.

On 20/04/2026 at 15:15 a trained production operator HA started manufacturing hydroxychloroquine sulphate 200mg/5ml oral suspension stock batch after line clearance which was carried out by trained line clearance operator WB and the volume check was performed by WB. After the volume check HA switched on the Silverson AX5 Asset No. 513 and began mixing. Shortly after starting up HA noticed a slight spark followed by a small puff of smoke from the rear of the Silverson along with a burning smell. HA immediately switched off the Silverson using the speed control knob and powered it down from the rear of the machine. HA then reported the incident to the production lead WB who was present at the time. When WB entered the bay WB also noticed a burning smell. As a precaution WB instructed HA to stop manufacturing. WB quarantined the product and the Silverson AX5 placed a Do Not Use label on the equipment and reported the incident to the Production Manager AA and Head of Department IP.
Beclometasone Dipropionate 0.0025% in White Soft Parrafin Cream
Instruction on BMR to use a 4-point balance not followed

On 23 Apr 2026 at approximately 18:15, during final release review of the Batch Manufacturing Record, the Final Release Officer identified that the required quantity of Beclometasone powder (13 mg) had been weighed using a 3-point balance and in grams, despite the approved BMR specifically instructing that the API must be weighed in milligrams using a 4-point balance. Investigation confirmed that the weighing was performed using an alternative method and equipment not specified within the approved manufacturing instructions. As the defined BMR requirement was not followed, the accuracy and appropriateness of the weighing step could not be assured in line with the approved process. Consequently, the batch was rejected at Final Release and deemed unsuitable for release.

Excessive foaming of Doxycycline Suspension product

On 24 Apr 2026, during Final Release assessment, a batch of Doxycycline 50 mg/5ml Oral Suspension was observed to exhibit excessive foam formation when shaken (see Appendix 1). As the product is a suspension, shaking prior to use is required to ensure even redistribution of the active ingredient and consistent dosing. However, when the bottle was shaken in accordance with normal use instructions, the batch generated an abnormal and persistent level of foam that was significantly greater than expected for this product.

During levomet powder blend mixing the V-MIXER start making noise and suddenly stop working as a precaution, we turned off switch and stopped manufacturing stock batch we quarantine the batch for now.

The deviation occurred due to equipment failure. The production technician FP identified an unusual noise coming from the VH mixer during powder blend mixing. FP promptly informed the team lead WB. When WB attended to inspect the equipment, the machine emitted several loud noises and then stopped operating.
In response, FP pressed the emergency stop button on machine and switched off the machine from the main power supply. Both the VH mixer and the powder blend have been placed under quarantine pending further investigation. A “Do Not Use” label has been placed on the VH-Mixer.

For the HPLC sequence HPLC4/2026/OMEPRAZOLE/05MAY/14MAY26_1 which was performed for the cleaning verification procedure for batch ES182047, the last injection of 100ppm Standard A had a peak area approximately 88% of the expected value, which caused the sequence precision to equate to 4.00% (in-house limit of 2.0% was exceeded).
Therefore, the system suitability test failed for the above sequence.

For the HPLC sequence HPLC4/2026/OMEPRAZOLE/05MAY/20MAY26_1 which was performed for the cleaning verification procedure for batch ES182304, the second injection of 100ppm Standard A had a peak area of 47.6951 mAU*min, whereas the first injection of 100ppm Standard A had a typical peak area of 78.3650 mAU*min.
Based on the atypically low peak area observed for the second 100 ppm Standard A injection, the sequence was stopped. Column performance was suspected; therefore, column COL048 was replaced with column COL040. 
The sequence was re-started with additional blank injections as part of a lengthy system equilibration period as column COL040 had not been used for any analysis since being cleaned with 0.1% Phosphoric Acid.
Overdue calibration on tinytag used to monitor humidty for tableting bay batches

Tinytag AN068 was identified as being used for Tableting Bay humidity monitoring beyond its calibration due date, while incorrectly recorded on the tracker as inactive/decommissioned. This is a repeat Tinytag calibration governance failure linked to CAPA.2025.017 effectiveness. Immediate containment and batch impact review completed; no humidity-related product impact identified. CAPA.2026.026 raised to strengthen tracker control, calibration governance, decommissioning controls, point-of-use checks, and fixed Comark monitoring.

On Friday 3rd July 2026, a site wide power outage resulted in temporary temperature excursions affecting four temperature controlled refrigerators used for the storage of pharmaceutical materials and products. The affected units were Dispatch Fridge 1, Dispatch Fridge 2, Production Fridge 1, and the QC Laboratory Fridge.
The power outgae caused each refrigerator to exceed its approved storage temperature range of 2–8°C for a limited duration. The recorded excursions were as follows:

Dispatch Fridge 1: 19:06–20:15 (approximately 69 minutes), maximum temperature 10.3°C.
Dispatch Fridge 2: 18:58–19:56 (approximately 58 minutes), maximum temperature 10.9°C.
Production Fridge 1: 19:14–20:00 (approximately 46 minutes), maximum temperature 10.5°C.
QC Laboratory Fridge: 19:26–19:53 (approximately 27 minutes), maximum temperature 9.0°C.

The excursion occurred because of the loss of electrical power, resulting in the refrigeration units being unable to maintain the validated storage temperature throughout the outage. Following restoration of power, normal operating temperatures were re-established. An assessment was initiated to identify all affected materials and products and to evaluate the potential impact of the excursions on product quality and to support product disposition in accordance with GMP requirements. See Appendix 1.

On 21 July 2026, QA Officer HK performed routine settle-plate environmental monitoring within the Grade D Manufacturing Cleanroom. The TSA plate corresponding to monitoring location Set-10, situated on the floor beneath the mirror in the clean-side change room, was reported by the contract microbiology laboratory, Quality Control North West (QCNW), as too numerous to count (TNTC).
QCNW reported that the TNTC result was attributable to spreading Bacillus growth around the edge of the plate. Thirty-six distinct colonies comprising Bacillus, Staphylococcus, unidentified Gram-positive rods and Micrococcus were observed. However, due to the spreading growth, an accurate total viable count could not be determined for the sample. All remaining TSA results were reported as complying with the established environmental-monitoring limits. All SDA results also complied with the established limits, with 4 CFU of mould recorded at the corresponding Set-10 location.
